title: Mitsubishi Electric Invests In Optical Quantum Computer Hardware Developer OptQC
excerpt: Mitsubishi Electric has invested in OptQC through its ME Innovation Fund, backing a Japanese startup developing optical quantum computer hardware designed for large-scale systems. Financial terms of the investment were not disclosed.
content:
By Amit Chowdhry Today at 1:29 AM

Mitsubishi Electric has invested in OptQC through its ME Innovation Fund, backing a Japanese startup developing optical quantum computer hardware designed for large-scale systems. Financial terms of the investment were not disclosed.

The transaction represents the ME Innovation Fund’s 16th investment and gives Mitsubishi Electric exposure to an emerging quantum computing architecture that could offer advantages in scalability and energy efficiency.

OptQC originated from the University of Tokyo and was established around technologies developed by the university’s Furusawa Laboratory, a research group focused on optical quantum computing.

Optical quantum computing uses photons as the basis for quantum information processing.

Mitsubishi Electric sees the approach as particularly promising as quantum computing moves from research toward industrial applications that could require substantially larger numbers of qubits.

One of the challenges associated with scaling quantum computers is that increasing the number of qubits can also significantly increase the physical size, complexity and energy requirements of the underlying hardware.

OptQC has developed a proprietary architecture intended to limit increases in system size as qubit counts rise.

The company believes that design could make its technology suitable for significantly larger quantum computing systems.

OptQC has already made progress toward commercial deployment.

The company has delivered its first commercial optical quantum computing system to a public research institution and has supplied hardware modules to private-sector companies.

For Mitsubishi Electric, the investment provides an opportunity to gain earlier visibility into OptQC’s technology development and the emerging commercial market around optical quantum computing.

The company expects to gain insights into OptQC’s hardware technologies, related components, customer requirements and broader quantum computing market trends.

Mitsubishi Electric plans to combine those insights with its own quantum technology capabilities, software implementation expertise and knowledge of industrial applications.

The strategy could eventually help Mitsubishi Electric identify new commercial opportunities as quantum computers become capable of addressing problems that are difficult or impractical for conventional computing systems.

Industrial quantum applications could eventually span areas such as optimization, materials development, simulation and other computationally intensive workloads.

Mitsubishi Electric’s investment also reflects growing corporate interest in quantum computing technologies as the industry attempts to move beyond laboratory demonstrations toward commercially useful systems.

OptQC’s focus on hardware scalability positions the company around one of the central technical challenges facing the industry.

Mitsubishi Electric said it aims to use the relationship to strengthen its position in quantum computing while developing potential new businesses around the technology.
